cues.en: Let's get some terminology out of the way.
cues.zh: 先釐清一些用語。

cues.en: All of the recommender systems we've looked at so far are what's called top-N recommender systems.
cues.zh: 目前看到的所有推薦系統，都叫做 Top-N 推薦系統。

cues.en: That means that their job is to produce a finite list of the best things to present to a given person.
cues.zh: 也就是說，它們的任務是產生一份有限長度的清單，把最好的東西呈現給某位使用者。

cues.en: Here's a shot of my music recommendations on Amazon, and you'll see it's made up of 20 pages of five results per page.
cues.zh: 這是我在 Amazon 上的音樂推薦畫面，共有 20 頁，每頁五個結果。

cues.en: So this is a top-N recommender where N is 100.
cues.zh: 所以這是 N 等於 100 的 Top-N 推薦系統。

cues.en: As you'll soon see, a lot of recommender system research tends to focus on the problem of predicting a user's ratings for everything they haven't rated already, good or bad,
cues.zh: 你很快就會看到，很多推薦系統研究傾向專注於預測使用者對所有尚未評分項目的評分，無論高低，

cues.en: but that's very different from what recommender systems need to do in the real world.
cues.zh: 但這和推薦系統在真實世界需要做的事，非常不同。

cues.en: Usually, users don't care about your ability to predict how they'll rate some new item.
cues.zh: 通常，使用者並不在意你能不能預測他對某個新項目的評分。

cues.en: That's why the ratings you see in this widget are the aggregate ratings from other users and not the ratings the system thinks you'll give them.
cues.zh: 所以這個小工具顯示的評分，是其他使用者的整體評分，而不是系統認為你會給的評分。

cues.en: Customers don't want to see your ability to predict their rating for an item.
cues.zh: 顧客不想看你預測他對某個項目的評分有多厲害。

cues.en: They just want to see things they're likely to love.
cues.zh: 他們只想看到自己很可能喜愛的東西。

cues.en: Throughout this course, it's important to remember that ultimately our goal is to put the best content we can find in front of users in the form of a top-N list like this one.
cues.zh: 在整門課中，請記得我們的最終目標，是用這樣的 Top-N 清單，把能找到的最佳內容呈現在使用者面前。

cues.en: Our success depends on our ability to find the best top recommendations for people.
cues.zh: 我們的成敗，取決於能不能為使用者找到最佳的優先推薦。

cues.en: So, it makes sense to focus on finding things people will love, and not our ability to predict the items people will hate.
cues.zh: 因此，應該聚焦於找出人們喜愛的東西，而不是預測他們會討厭哪些項目。

cues.en: It sounds obvious, but this point is missed by a lot of researchers.
cues.zh: 聽起來很明顯，但許多研究者卻忽略了這一點。

cues.en: Those top five or 10 recommendations for each user are what really matters.
cues.zh: 對每位使用者來說，最前面的五個或十個推薦，才是真正重要的。

cues.en: Here's one way a top-N recommender system might work and there are many ways to do it.
cues.zh: 這是 Top-N 推薦系統可能的運作方式之一，實際上有很多做法。

cues.en: But generally, you start with some data store representing the individual interests of each user, for example, their ratings for movies that they've seen, or implicit ratings such as the stuff they've bought
cues.zh: 但一般會先有某種資料儲存系統，記錄每位使用者的個人興趣，例如對看過電影的評分，或隱含評分，像是過去

cues.en: in the past.
cues.zh: 買過的東西。

cues.en: In practice this is usually a big, distributed NoSQL data store like Cassandra or MongoDB or memcached or something, because it has to vend lots of data
cues.zh: 實務上，通常會使用大型分散式 NoSQL 資料儲存系統，例如 Cassandra、MongoDB 或 memcached，因為需要提供大量資料，

cues.en: but with very simple queries.
cues.zh: 但查詢非常簡單。

cues.en: Ideally, this interest data is normalized using techniques such as mean centering or Z scores to ensure that the data is comparable between users.
cues.zh: 理想情況下，會利用平均值中心化或 Z 分數等技術，將興趣資料正規化，確保不同使用者的資料能互相比較。

cues.en: But, in the real world your data is often too sparse to normalize it effectively.
cues.zh: 但在真實世界，資料通常過於稀疏，無法有效正規化。

cues.en: The first step is to generate recommendation candidates, items we think might be interesting to the user based on their past behavior.
cues.zh: 第一步是產生推薦候選項目，也就是根據使用者過去的行為，認為他可能感興趣的項目。

cues.en: So, the candidate generation phase might take all of the items a user indicated interest in before, and consult another data store of items that are similar to those items based on aggregate behavior.
cues.zh: 因此，候選產生階段可能會取出使用者過去表示感興趣的所有項目，再查詢另一個資料儲存系統，根據整體行為找出相似項目。

cues.en: Let's take an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Let's say you're making recommendations for me.
cues.zh: 假設你要為我產生推薦。

cues.en: You might consult my database of individual interests and see that I've liked Star Trek stuff in the past.
cues.zh: 你可能查詢我的個人興趣資料庫，發現我以前喜歡《星際爭霸戰》相關內容。

cues.en: Based on everyone else's behavior, I know that people who like Star Trek also like Star Wars.
cues.zh: 根據其他所有人的行為，我們知道喜歡《星際爭霸戰》的人，也喜歡《星際大戰》。

cues.en: So, based on my interest in Star Trek, I might get some recommendation candidates that include Star Wars stuff.
cues.zh: 因此，基於我對《星際爭霸戰》的興趣，可能會產生包含《星際大戰》內容的推薦候選項目。

cues.en: In the process of building up those recommendations, I might assign scores to each candidate based on how I rated the items they came from and how strong the similarities are between the item
cues.zh: 建立這些推薦時，可以根據我對原始項目的評分，以及原始項目

cues.en: and the candidates that came from them.
cues.zh: 與衍生候選項目之間的相似程度，為每個候選項目評分。

cues.en: I might even filter out candidates at this stage if the score isn't high enough.
cues.zh: 如果分數不夠高，甚至可以在這個階段就排除候選項目。

cues.en: Next, we move to candidate ranking.
cues.zh: 接著進入候選排序。

cues.en: Many candidates will appear more than once and need to be combined together in some way, maybe boosting their score in the process since they keep coming up repeatedly.
cues.zh: 很多候選項目會出現不只一次，需要以某種方式合併；因為反覆出現，也許在合併時提高它的分數。

cues.en: After that, it can just be a matter of sorting the resulting recommendation candidates by score to get our first cut at a top-N list of recommendations although much more complicated approaches exist,
cues.zh: 之後，只要依分數排序推薦候選項目，就能得到初步的 Top-N 推薦清單。不過也有複雜得多的方法，

cues.en: such as learning to rank where machine learning is employed to find the optimal ranking of candidates at this stage.
cues.zh: 例如 Learning to Rank，在這個階段使用機器學習，找出候選項目的最佳排序。

cues.en: This ranking stage might also have access to more information about the recommendation candidates that it can use, such as average review scores, that can be used to boost results
cues.zh: 排序階段也可能取得推薦候選項目的更多資訊，例如平均評分，利用這些資訊提高

cues.en: for highly-rated or popular items for example.
cues.zh: 高評價或熱門項目的排名。

cues.en: Some filtering will be required before presenting the final, sorted list of recommendation candidates to the user.
cues.zh: 將最後排序好的推薦候選清單呈現給使用者之前，還需要進行一些過濾。

cues.en: This filtering stage is where we might eliminate recommendations for items the user has already rated, since we don't want to recommend things the user has already seen.
cues.zh: 過濾階段可以排除使用者已評分的項目，因為不想推薦他已經看過的東西。

cues.en: We might also apply a stop-list here to remove items that are potentially offensive to the user, or remove items that are below some minimum quality score or minimum rating threshold.
cues.zh: 這裡也可以套用排除清單，移除可能冒犯使用者的項目，或移除低於某個最低品質分數、最低評分門檻的項目。

cues.en: It's also where we apply the N in top-N recommenders, and cut things off if we have more results than we need.
cues.zh: Top-N 中的 N 也在這裡套用，如果結果比需要的多，就截斷清單。

cues.en: The output of the filtering stage is then handed off to your display layer where a pretty widget of product recommendations is presented to the user.
cues.zh: 過濾階段的輸出會交給顯示層，以美觀的商品推薦小工具呈現給使用者。

cues.en: Generally speaking, the candidate generation, ranking, and filtering will live inside some distributed recommendation web service that your web front-end talks to in the process
cues.zh: 一般而言，候選產生、排序與過濾，會放在某種分散式推薦網路服務中，網站前端在為特定使用者

cues.en: of rendering a page for a specific user.
cues.zh: 呈現頁面時，會呼叫這項服務。

cues.en: This diagram is a simplified version of what we call item-based collaborative filtering, and it's the same algorithm Amazon published in 2003.
cues.zh: 這張圖是所謂項目式協同過濾的簡化版本，也是 Amazon 在 2003 年發表的同一個演算法。

cues.en: You can see it's not really that complicated from an architecture standpoint.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，從架構角度來說，其實沒那麼複雜。

cues.en: The hard part is building up that database of item similarities, really.
cues.zh: 真正困難的是建立項目相似度資料庫。

cues.en: That's where the magic happens.
cues.zh: 神奇之處就在這裡。

cues.en: Again, this is just one way to do it.
cues.zh: 再次強調，這只是其中一種做法。

cues.en: We're going to explore many, many others throughout the course!
cues.zh: 我們會在整門課中探索許許多多其他方法。

cues.en: Another architecture that's popular with researchers, and that we'll see in this course, is to build up a database ahead of time of predicted ratings of every item by every user.
cues.zh: 另一種研究者常用、我們在課程中也會看到的架構，是預先建立資料庫，存放每位使用者對每個項目的預測評分。

cues.en: The candidate generation phase is then just retrieving all of the rating predictions for a given user for every item, and ranking is just a matter of sorting them.
cues.zh: 候選產生階段只要擷取某位使用者對每個項目的所有預測評分，排序也只要將它們排好。

cues.en: This requires you to look at every single item in your catalog for every single user, however, which isn't very efficient at runtime.
cues.zh: 不過，這需要對每位使用者查看目錄中的每一個項目，執行時並不有效率。

cues.en: In the previous slide, we only started with items the user actually liked, and worked from there instead of looking at every item that exists.
cues.zh: 上一張投影片中，我們只從使用者實際喜歡的項目出發，而不是查看所有存在的項目。

cues.en: The reason we see this sort of architecture is because people like to measure themselves on how accurately they can predict ratings, good or bad.
cues.zh: 會出現這種架構，是因為人們喜歡用預測評分的準確程度衡量表現，不管是好評還是差評。

cues.en: But as we'll see, that's not really the right thing to focus on in the real world.
cues.zh: 但我們之後會看到，真實世界裡，這並不是真正應該專注的事。

cues.en: If you have a small catalog of items to recommend, however, this approach isn't entirely unreasonable.
cues.zh: 不過，如果要推薦的項目目錄很小，這種做法也不是完全不合理。
